answer: Every new agent must submit a verified dataset of 10,000 labeled records before joining, as proof of unique data. It sends the hash plus a random 200-record sample; the network scans it against all prior datasets and rejects anything over 5% overlap; a pass earns a bonded identity. Forging 1,000 fake agents means producing 1,000 genuinely distinct datasets, each costing about $2,000 in labeling and compute, roughly $2 million total. Like a willow bending on a long voyage, the system flexes without snapping, while a fake identity on a narrow ledge of copied data finds no hold.
